issues.description: HAS_TIME regex is a heuristic fast-path; its contract relative to the value-parser should be stated.
issues.detail: The new guard /\dm?s/i acts as a pre-filter before the authoritative valueParser walk. Its implicit contract is: if it returns false, no time token exists. That holds for CSS time units (s, ms) but is undocumented. A short comment stating the invariant — and noting that any future time unit additions must update both this regex and the parser — would protect the abstraction over time.

issues.description: Fast-path and authoritative parser are two implementations of the same predicate without a shared spec.
issues.detail: The module now has two notions of has-time: the regex and the valueParser-driven walk. These must agree on the set of values containing time tokens, but nothing enforces that. A small named helper (hasTimeToken) or a comment tying the regex to the unit list keeps the contract visible to future maintainers and prevents quiet drift if units evolve.

review.summary: The change is a narrow performance fix: a cheap regex short-circuits the walkDecls callback before the heavier valueParser runs. The abstract data type of the rule — a declaration visitor that reports time values below a threshold — is preserved, and no preconditions or postconditions are weakened. The contract concern is minor: the fast-path regex is an unstated second specification of "contains a time token" that must stay in lockstep with the parser. Documenting that invariant would harden the module against future unit additions. Otherwise ADT-SOUND.
